# Grain — Style Reference

> Frosted glass on a meeting-room whiteboard with one emerald marker. Poppins semibold headlines in soft graphite, Inter body text on a five-step grey ladder, white canvas, eight-pixel corners, translucent hairlines, and a single emerald #009959 fill.

**Theme:** light

Values are measured from the live site and normalized; names, roles and recommendations are interpretation. Font lists are independent, not paired by position. Example prompts describe reconstructions, not the site's source code.

Grain speaks a frosted-whiteboard product language. The canvas is #ffffff, chapters below the hero sit on #fafafa bands divided by hairlines, icons rest in #f0f0f0 tiles, and secondary buttons are #ffffff66 glass that lets a pale mint backdrop tint through. The chromatic budget is exactly one hue. Emerald #009959 is permitted on the primary CTA fill, on the single green word inside the H1, and on the active feature-tab ring, and nowhere else. Every other pixel sits on a grey ladder from #000000 down to #949494. Typography splits the labor. Poppins 600 carries all hierarchy at 60px, 42px and 28px in a softened #313232, with -1px tracking at display size. Inter 400 handles reading at 16px and 18px, and the 60/18 jump of 3.33× means size, not weight, separates headline from text. Shape is rounded-soft: 8px buttons and 16px and 24px cards. Elevation is a 4% black breath rather than a lift. The page reads as a calm workspace rather than a sales floor.

## Tokens — Colors

| Name | Value | Token | Role |
|---|---|---|---|
| Paper Canvas | `#ffffff` | `--color-paper-canvas` | Body background, stat-card fill, screenshot frames and label text on emerald. This is the white page that every grey and the single green are measured against. |
| Fog Wash | `#fafafa` | `--color-fog-wash` | Alternating section bands below the hero and the "Universal capture" chapter. A 2% tonal step marks a new chapter without introducing a new color. |
| Mist Tile | `#f0f0f0` | `--color-mist-tile` | The 48px icon wells in feature cards and the eyebrow icon chips (4 uses). It creates a recessed grey pocket that holds monochrome icons without needing a border. |
| Frosted Glass | `#ffffff66` | `--color-frosted-glass` | Secondary "Book my demo" fill and glass panels over the mint hero wash. At 40% white the backdrop tints through, so outline buttons float instead of sitting flat. |
| Onyx | `#000000` | `--color-onyx` | FAQ accordion triggers, footer copy and the wordmark (29 uses). Pure black is reserved for structural text that persists, never headlines. Do not use it for Poppins display type. |
| Jet Ink | `#141414` | `--color-jet-ink` | Nav links, button labels and FAQ questions (32 uses, the most frequent text color). This is the workhorse ink, a hair off black so 14px UI text never vibrates against white. |
| Graphite Heading | `#313232` | `--color-graphite-heading` | Every Poppins H1 and H2 plus card body inheritance (12 uses). It is deliberately lighter than the UI ink, so 600-weight geometric headlines are heavy in shape but soft in tone. |
| Slate Body | `#545454` | `--color-slate-body` | The hero lede and section subheads at 18px (16 uses). This is the reading grey, at roughly 7.5:1 contrast, clearly subordinate to the headline graphite. |
| Ash Caption | `#707070` | `--color-ash-caption` | Feature-card copy, tab descriptions and eyebrow labels (16 uses). It sits at roughly 4.9:1 contrast, the floor for any sentence a visitor must actually read. |
| Pebble Muted | `#949494` | `--color-pebble-muted` | Trust-badge text, 24px icons, the logo-row tint and the hero secondary border (9 uses). It is decorative-weight grey. Do not set paragraphs in it, because it falls near 3:1 contrast. |
| Quartz Border | `#c9c9c9` | `--color-quartz-border` | The 1px edge on the nav "Book my demo" button and other outline controls. It is the only opaque border grey, strong enough to define a button on glass. |
| Dove Hairline | `#0000001a` | `--color-dove-hairline` | Trust-badge outlines and section dividers at 10% black. A translucent hairline reads identically on #ffffff, #fafafa and the mint wash. |
| Emerald Signal | `#009959` | `--color-emerald-signal` | Primary CTA fill, the word "agents" in the H1, and the active feature-tab border. These 5 placements are the system's entire chromatic budget. Do not use it on secondary buttons, icons or section backgrounds. |

## Tokens — Typography

### Poppins — geometric semibold display face that carries every headline · `--font-poppins`

- **Substitute:** Poppins itself at 600 (Google Fonts, identical); Outfit at 700, because Outfit draws lighter than Poppins at equal weight and 700 matches the stroke; Plus Jakarta Sans at 700, which is narrower, so expect slightly tighter line breaks.
- **Weights:** 600
- **Sizes:** 20px, 28px, 42px, 52px, 60px
- **Line height:** 1.04, 1.1, 1.25, 1.6
- **Letter spacing:** -1px at 60px, -1.04px at 52px, 0 at 42px, 0 at 28px, -0.4px at 20px
- **Role:** A single weight across five sizes is the signature. Poppins never goes bolder or lighter, so its round bowls and flat terminals do the branding while size alone ranks importance. The display-to-section step (60/42 = 1.43) is steeper than a Perfect Fourth (1.333), which gives the H1 a poster quality the rest of the page never repeats. Tightening only the top two sizes, -1px at 60px and -1.04px at 52px, corrects the geometric face's loose default fit where it matters and leaves the 42px H2s at their natural spacing.

### Inter Variable — neutral grotesk that does all reading and all interface work · `--font-inter-variable`

- **Substitute:** Inter at 400, 500 and 600 (Google Fonts, the same design); Geist at 400 for body, which matches Inter's color closely; Instrument Sans at 400, which reads marginally darker, so do not raise it to 500 for body.
- **Weights:** 400, 500, 600
- **Sizes:** 13px, 14px, 16px, 18px, 20px, 32px
- **Line height:** 1.23, 1.43, 1.5, 1.6
- **Letter spacing:** -0.36px at 18px (weight 400), -0.54px at 18px (weight 600), -0.32px at 16px, -0.4px at 20px, 0 at 13px and 14px
- **Role:** Inter is the workhorse at 110 measured uses against Poppins's 16. Weight 400 is 73 of those uses, and 500 appears almost exclusively on buttons, so medium weight means "clickable" here rather than "important". Body steps are tight (14 → 16 → 18, a 1.125 ratio, below a Minor Third), which keeps paragraphs, labels and tabs in one quiet register under the Poppins headlines. Negative tracking appears only at 16px and above, a small optical correction that keeps the lede from looking airy next to the denser geometric headings.

### Type Scale

| Role | Family | Weight | Size | Line Height | Letter Spacing | Token |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| small | Inter Variable | 500 | 13px | 1.23 | 0px | `--text-small` |
| caption | Inter Variable | 500 | 14px | 1.43 | 0px | `--text-caption` |
| body-sm | Inter Variable | 400 | 14px | 1.43 | 0px | `--text-body-sm` |
| body | Inter Variable | 400 | 16px | 1.5 | 0px | `--text-body` |
| body-lg | Inter Variable | 400 | 18px | 1.5 | -0.36px | `--text-body-lg` |
| subheading | Inter Variable | 600 | 18px | 1.6 | -0.54px | `--text-subheading` |
| heading-sm | Poppins | 600 | 20px | 1.6 | -0.4px | `--text-heading-sm` |
| heading | Poppins | 600 | 28px | 1.6 | 0px | `--text-heading` |
| heading-lg | Poppins | 600 | 42px | 1.25 | 0px | `--text-heading-lg` |
| display | Poppins | 600 | 60px | 1.04 | -1px | `--text-display` |

## Do's and Don'ts

### Do

- Spend #009959 on one filled button per viewport plus the single emphasized H1 word — scarcity is what makes the green read as "go".
- Set every H1 and H2 in Poppins 600 at #313232, never in #000000 — the softened graphite tames the heavy geometric stroke.
- Rank hierarchy by size (60px → 42px → 28px) and keep Poppins at weight 600 throughout — one weight, many sizes, is the typographic signature.
- Use the grey ladder in order: #141414 for UI labels, #545454 for the lede, #707070 for card copy, #949494 for badges — each step has a single job.
- Hold buttons at an 8px radius and cards at 16px or 24px — the system softens as objects grow, so actions stay the crispest shapes on screen.
- Separate sections with a #fafafa band or a 1px #0000001a hairline at 96px rhythm — tonal steps and lines replace dark blocks.
- Cap shadows at `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.08) 0px 4px 16px 0px` and reserve that level for screenshots and floating callouts — weight goes to what deserves inspection.

### Don't

- Don't add a second brand hue for icons, tags or hover states (a purple or blue at 100% saturation) — Grain's identity is the single emerald, and a second color splits the CTA's monopoly.
- Don't tint the secondary button or the feature cards with #009959 at 10% to "carry the brand" — green surfaces dilute the one conversion signal into wallpaper.
- Don't bold Inter body copy to 600 for emphasis inside 16px paragraphs — weight 600 belongs to 18px tab titles, and in-paragraph bolding creates a third hierarchy channel the system never uses.
- Don't push the 24px card radius to 9999px pills on buttons — the 8px action corner against the softer 24px card corner is the shape contrast that tells a visitor what to click.
- Don't set long paragraphs in #949494 because it "looks lighter" — at about 3:1 contrast it fails body readability, and #707070 is the floor.
- Don't stack heavy elevation like `0 20px 40px` at 25% black on cards — the 4% to 8% shadow range is non-negotiable, and deeper shadows turn fog into plastic.
- Don't let partner or customer logos keep their full color in the marquee or integrations row — never spend the page's chromatic budget on another brand's palette.

## Agent Prompt Guide

**Quick Color Reference**

- background: #ffffff (Paper Canvas)
- section band: #fafafa (Fog Wash)
- headline text: #313232 (Graphite Heading)
- UI text: #141414 (Jet Ink)
- body text: #545454 (Slate Body)
- secondary text: #707070 (Ash Caption)
- border: #c9c9c9 (Quartz Border)
- primary action: #009959 (filled action)

**Color in Data**

Charts use neutral bars in #c9c9c9 and #949494, with #009959 applied as a solid fill to the single series that represents the user's outcome, so the data never contains more green than the page's primary button.

**Example Component Prompts**

1. Build a primary action button labeled "Get started free": background #009959, text #ffffff, Inter Variable 14px weight 500, line height 1.43, letter spacing 0px, padding 16px 32px, height 54px, border none, border-radius 8px, box-shadow none. On hover keep the same fill and add the shadow `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.04) 0px 4px 8px 0px`. Place it left of a secondary button at a 16px gap. The secondary uses background #ffffff66, text #141414, a 1px solid #949494 border, the same 8px radius, 16px 32px padding and Inter 14px weight 500.

2. Build a hero section on #ffffff with a decorative pale-mint radial wash behind it, inside a 1200px container with 96px top padding. Use a two-column grid with a 48px gap. In the left column, place a row of two trust items in Inter 14px weight 400 #949494, then an H1 in Poppins 600 at 60px, line height 1.04, letter spacing -1px, color #313232, with the word "agents" colored #009959. Below the H1 set a 24px gap and an 18px Inter weight 400 lede in #545454 (line height 1.5, letter spacing -0.36px, max-width 480px), then a 32px gap and the primary and secondary button pair, then 16px of checkmark reassurances in Inter 13px weight 400 #545454. In the right column, place a product screenshot in a #ffffff frame with a 14px radius and shadow `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.08) 0px 4px 16px 0px`.

3. Build a four-up feature card row under a centered Poppins 600 42px H2 (#313232, line height 1.25). Each card is 300px wide and 285px tall with a transparent background, no border, a 24px radius, 40px 24px padding and shadow `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.04) 0px 4px 8px 0px`. Center a 48px square icon tile (#f0f0f0, 12px radius, 24px #949494 line icon) at the top, then a 24px gap, then two lines of centered Inter Variable 16px weight 400 #707070 at line height 1.5. Separate the cards with a 20px gap.

4. Build a sticky navigation bar 80px tall with a #ffffff background and no shadow, inside a 1200px container. On the left, place a 90px-wide wordmark, a 32px gap, then the links Product, Use Cases, Resources and Pricing in Inter Variable 14px weight 400 #141414, each with 8px padding and an 8px gap. Add a 1px #0000001a vertical divider 24px tall, then "Grain for Sales" in the same style. On the right, use an 8px gap between three actions. "Sign In" is transparent with #141414 Inter 14px weight 500, 12px 16px padding and an 8px radius. "Book my demo" is #ffffff66 with a 1px #c9c9c9 border, 12px 16px padding and an 8px radius. "Get started free" is #009959 with #ffffff text, 12px 16px padding and an 8px radius.

### Feature Card — Frosted Pillar

**Role:** Four-up value propositions under H2

The main content card. **Role:** Quantified proof points

Solid and slightly crisper. The spec is a #ffffff background, no border, a 16px radius, 32px 28px padding, a 348px × 230px footprint, and shadow `rgba(16, 24, 40, 0.04) 0px 1px 2px 0px`. Body text is Inter Variable 16px weight 400 in #313232, and the counter figure is set in Poppins 600 at 42px. The tighter 16px radius and the 1px-offset shadow make it sit closer to the page than the 24px feature card, as befits numbers that ask to be believed rather than imagined.

### Trust Badge — Hairline Chip

**Role:** Compliance and review signals

Small and quiet. The spec is a transparent background, #949494 text in Inter Variable 16px weight 400, a 1px #0000001a border on the compliance variants (SOC 2, GDPR) and none on the review variants, a 6px radius, 8px padding, a 39px height, and a 16px #949494 leading icon. The badges are deliberately low-contrast, so they register as fine print that certifies rather than as buttons that solicit. The review stars carry an orange tint that is decorative and not a system token.

### Section Eyebrow — Icon Label

**Role:** Names each feature chapter

A whisper above the headline. A 24px #f0f0f0 chip with a 6px radius holds a 16px monochrome icon, followed at an 8px gap by the label ("Universal capture", "Context for AI") in Inter Variable 13px weight 500, line height 1.23, #707070. A 16px gap separates it from the Poppins 42px H2 below. Where convention would use an uppercase tracked kicker or a colored pill, Grain uses sentence-case grey, which keeps the emerald budget intact.

### Feature Tab Stack — Vertical Selector

**Role:** Switches the adjacent product screenshot

Stacked and selective. Each tab is a #ffffff panel with a 12px radius and 16px 20px padding, titled in Inter Variable 18px weight 600 (-0.54px tracking, #141414) above Inter Variable 16px weight 400 in #707070. The active tab gains a 1px #009959 border and full opacity, while inactive tabs drop to a faded state with only a right-edge hairline. This ring is the only place emerald appears as a border, which makes "selected" and "go" the same color by design.

### Product Screenshot Frame

**Role:** The site's primary imagery

Real UI, lightly framed. The spec is a #ffffff panel with a 14px radius, shadow `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.08) 0px 4px 16px 0px`, and no border. A window chrome strip carries three traffic-light dots whose red, amber and green are mockup-internal and not system tokens. Inside, the product's own typography and colored timeline bars are left untouched. The frame is the heaviest shadow in the system because it is the one object meant to be studied closely.

### Floating Callout — Overlay Widget

**Role:** Annotates screenshots with a claim

Perched and overlapping. The callout is a #ffffff card with a 16px radius, 20px padding and shadow `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.08) 0px 4px 16px 0px`. It breaks the screenshot's top edge by roughly 24px (estimated). Its title is Inter Variable 14px weight 600 #141414, a body line is Inter 14px weight 400 #545454, and a row of 24px partner glyphs completes it (third-party logos, not system tokens). It is the system outlier in composition, the only element allowed to overlap another, and it exists to tie the screenshot to the "agents" story.

### Logo Marquee Row

**Role:** Social proof strip

Monochrome and continuous. A Poppins 600 28px heading in #313232 introduces a horizontally scrolling row of customer wordmarks, all flattened to a #949494 grey at roughly 24px cap height, with 48px gaps and soft fade masks at both ends (estimated). The row sits inside the mint hero wash before the first hairline. Desaturating every partner logo keeps third-party brand colors from spending Grain's single-hue budget on someone else.

### FAQ Accordion

**Role:** Closing objections before the footer

Bare rows. The accordion sits in an 864px-wide column with 45px trigger rows. Questions are set in Inter Variable 18px weight 400 #141414 within a #000000 container and divided by #0000001a hairlines. There are no backgrounds, no radius and no shadow, and the plus/chevron icon is 24px #949494. Where most SaaS FAQs box each item, Grain's open-list treatment lets the page end in text rather than chrome.

## Do's and Don'ts

### Do

- Spend #009959 on one filled button per viewport plus the single emphasized H1 word — scarcity is what makes the green read as "go".
- Set every H1 and H2 in Poppins 600 at #313232, never in #000000 — the softened graphite tames the heavy geometric stroke.
- Rank hierarchy by size (60px → 42px → 28px) and keep Poppins at weight 600 throughout — one weight, many sizes, is the typographic signature.
- Use the grey ladder in order: #141414 for UI labels, #545454 for the lede, #707070 for card copy, #949494 for badges — each step has a single job.
- Hold buttons at an 8px radius and cards at 16px or 24px — the system softens as objects grow, so actions stay the crispest shapes on screen.
- Separate sections with a #fafafa band or a 1px #0000001a hairline at 96px rhythm — tonal steps and lines replace dark blocks.
- Cap shadows at `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.08) 0px 4px 16px 0px` and reserve that level for screenshots and floating callouts — weight goes to what deserves inspection.

### Don't

- Don't add a second brand hue for icons, tags or hover states (a purple or blue at 100% saturation) — Grain's identity is the single emerald, and a second color splits the CTA's monopoly.
- Don't tint the secondary button or the feature cards with #009959 at 10% to "carry the brand" — green surfaces dilute the one conversion signal into wallpaper.
- Don't bold Inter body copy to 600 for emphasis inside 16px paragraphs — weight 600 belongs to 18px tab titles, and in-paragraph bolding creates a third hierarchy channel the system never uses.
- Don't push the 24px card radius to 9999px pills on buttons — the 8px action corner against the softer 24px card corner is the shape contrast that tells a visitor what to click.
- Don't set long paragraphs in #949494 because it "looks lighter" — at about 3:1 contrast it fails body readability, and #707070 is the floor.
- Don't stack heavy elevation like `0 20px 40px` at 25% black on cards — the 4% to 8% shadow range is non-negotiable, and deeper shadows turn fog into plastic.
- Don't let partner or customer logos keep their full color in the marquee or integrations row — never spend the page's chromatic budget on another brand's palette.

## Elevation

- **Feature cards (24px radius):** `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.04) 0px 4px 8px 0px`
- **Stat cards (16px radius):** `rgba(16, 24, 40, 0.04) 0px 1px 2px 0px`
- **Product screenshot frames and floating callouts:** `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.08) 0px 4px 16px 0px`
- **Pressed or recessed wells, single instance:** `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.05) 0px 0px 12px 0px inset`

The rule is that no shadow exceeds 8% opacity or a 16px blur. Where Material-style systems escalate to 24dp-style drops, Grain's elevation is a tint of air. The heaviest value is spent on product imagery, so screenshots appear to rest a few millimeters above the page while every other object stays flush.

## Imagery

Imagery is almost entirely real product UI: meeting summaries, transcript views, timeline scrubbers and a video-call grid, each shown inside a #ffffff frame with a 14px radius and the 8% md shadow. Photography appears only inside those mockups as participant video tiles and 32px circular avatars, never as standalone lifestyle photos. Icons are 16px and 24px monochrome line glyphs in #949494 or #313232, housed in #f0f0f0 tiles with 12px or 6px radii. The hero sits on a soft mint-to-white radial gradient that is decorative only and not a system token. The logo mark's lighter green (#00b96c) is likewise decorative and confined to the wordmark. Saturated timeline bars inside screenshots are mockup-internal. The narrative is "this is what your meetings look like after Grain", argued by showing the product rather than by illustration.

## Layout

Content sits in a 1200px container inside a 1600px outer frame, with chapters spaced at 96px and divided by #fafafa bands or #0000001a hairlines. The hero is a two-column split: on the left, a review row, a 60px Poppins H1, an 18px lede, a CTA pair and checkmark reassurances; on the right, a large product screenshot with an overlapping callout. A full-width logo marquee follows, then a centered H2 with a four-column feature-card grid. Feature chapters alternate an eyebrow plus a left-aligned 42px H2 with a two-column body that pairs a vertical tab stack with a screenshot, swapping sides between chapters. Stat cards run three across, and the FAQ narrows to 864px. The nav is sticky, 80px tall and filled white, with the logo and links on the left and the three actions on the right. The footer is a 48px-padded text grid on white. At 375px, set display at 42px, set section gaps at 72px, and stack every grid to one column. Overall density: comfortable.

## Emerald Rationing

Grain's discipline is a one-hue budget. Emerald #009959 appears on 3 fills, 1 word and 1 border across the entire home page, and every other chromatic moment (the logo's #00b96c, review stars, screenshot timelines) is either decorative or mockup-internal. Three changes would break it: a colored icon set, a green-tinted card background, or a second accent for "new" badges. Any one of them turns the CTA from the only signal into one signal among several. To extend the system, express new states through the grey ladder and the shape vocabulary first. Success, info and warning states should use #313232 text with a #0000001a hairline and an icon, and only a true commit action earns a #009959 fill. If a status color becomes unavoidable, keep it below 12px in size and away from button shapes.

## Grey Ladder Discipline

Six neutrals each own exactly one job. #000000 is for structure, #141414 for UI labels, #313232 for display headlines, #545454 for lede paragraphs, #707070 for card copy and #949494 for badges and icons. The inversion is deliberate: headlines at #313232 are lighter than 14px nav text at #141414, because Poppins 600 at 42px already carries enough mass. The ladder breaks when a builder picks greys by eye, adding a #666666 here or a #888888 there, or darkens headlines to pure black for "impact", which turns the semibold geometric face into a shout. To extend the system, map every new text role onto an existing rung by function and size. If nothing fits, the role is redundant and should reuse the nearest rung.

## Screenshot as Hero

Grain illustrates nothing. Every visual argument is a real product screen in a 14px-radius white frame carrying the system's heaviest shadow (8% black, 16px blur). That is the anti-convention choice in a category where competitors lean on abstract waveforms and AI glow orbs. The discipline breaks when decorative 3D renders, gradient blobs or stock photography of people in meetings replace UI. It also breaks when screenshots are given colored device frames, thick borders or tilted perspective that competes with the flat page. To extend the system, capture new features at the same 14px radius with light window chrome. Annotate them with a single white floating callout (16px radius, md shadow) rather than arrows or highlights, and let the product's own interface supply any color.

## Similar Brands

- **Grain** — Like Otter.ai, it markets an AI meeting notetaker through full product screenshots of transcripts and summaries, but it restricts its accent to one emerald where Otter spreads blue across icons and illustrations.
- **Grain** — Shares Loom's two-button hero (solid brand fill beside a quiet outline) and screenshot-led storytelling, with Poppins 600 in place of Loom's heavier custom grotesk.
- **Grain** — Matches Attio's near-monochrome canvas with translucent 10%-black hairlines and sub-10% shadows, while running warmer, rounder geometry (24px cards versus Attio's tighter corners).
- **Grain** — Uses Notion's strategy of a neutral grey ladder with color reserved for the product's own content, though Grain commits to a single green CTA where Notion's marketing rotates accents.
- **Grain** — Competes with Fireflies.ai in the same category but inverts its approach, replacing gradient-heavy, multi-hue AI imagery with a frosted white surface and one rationed green.
